newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines seen re-entering wheat market - trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippines seen re-entering wheat market - trade.

text.p: Philippine wheat importers are expected to come back into the market this week on any price dips, Manila-based importers said on Monday.
Ample supplies will keep the market for corn, rice, soybeans and soymeal quiet, the importers said.
Traders said they have received inquiries from three millers for a total of 65,000 tonnes of wheat for May or June shipment.
"We have offered them U.S. wheat but they rejected all prices because they said these were too high," one trader said.
Another trader said buyers have informed him they would wait for prices to soften before firming up their orders.
"If U.S. wheat prices stay at current price levels, the buyers may look at other origins like Canada," the trader said.

But any prospect of easier prices now appears unlikely. Prices in Minneapolis, where the Philippines buys most of its wheat, rose on Friday with the MGE May contract finishing 7-1/4 U.S. cents up at US$4.30 a bushel.
Harsh winter-like weather during springtime in the U.S. plus dry weather in Europe have lifted world wheat prices.
Hog growers in the Philippines repeated their request to the Agriculture Department to import an additional 300,000 tonnes of corn for animal feed.

The National Federation of Hog Farmers said a corn shortage could touch 1.2 million tonnes this year. Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero has said the Philippines will probably import only 500,000 tonnes of corn in 1997.
Philippine flour prices remained steady at 290 pesos per 25-kg bag for hard flour and 260 pesos per 25-kg bag for soft flour.
